newsitem.title: UK: Iraq, Nigerian crudes set to loosen Urals' grip.
newsitem.headline: Iraq, Nigerian crudes set to loosen Urals' grip.

text.p: A dearth of prompt Urals supplies helped to counter pressure from Iraqi and West African barrels and limp refinery demand in the Mediterranean sour crude market, traders said on Monday.
"The (Med) market is by no means strong. It's feeling the pressure from West Africa -- which is a dog -- and Brent is getting sold at a big discount to the screen." said one trader.
Nevertheless, traders said Urals held steady on Friday's talked levels in the Dated Brent minus 90 cents area, because of a lack of prompt barrels.
Urals has a much shorter nomination period than most crudes, selling just a few days ahead of loading.
"There aren't many prompt avails," said one trader. "The few that have prompt barrels for sale are talking in the (Dated Brent) -95/90 range."
But local refiners said that Urals was set to weaken under competition from other crudes in a market shrunk by seasonal refinery maintenance.
"It's the maintenance season at the moment, I see differentials falling to (Dated Brent) -$1.30 to -$1.40 in the next week," said one Med refiner.
Supplies of Iraqi Kirkuk were seen plentiful although no spot availabilities were actively offered by traders.
"There are still Iraqi barrels around, if you want to buy you can buy direct from (Iraqi state marketer) SOMO," said one contract lifter.
Shipping costs of Worldscale 110 for one million barrel cargoes from the Turkish port of Ceyhan, where Kirkuk loads, to the Mediterranean were stifling trade, dealers said.
A crumbling West African crude market also added to supply pressures in the Mediterranean.

Traders estimated that 23 to 24 million March-loading barrels from the Nigerian programme were still unsold. Med refiners said they were offered a range of grades from heating oil-rich Forcados to lighter Brass River and Bonny Light.

A late-March loading Forcados was traded on Friday at a discount to Dated Brent, compared to the March official selling price (OSP) of Dated Brent +47 cents -- the level at which contract lifters are obliged buy cargoes.
"With Nigerian (crudes) at a discount there are no sours that can compete with those grades," said one refiner.
At least one contract lifter was heard moving West African barrels to the Mediterranean to put in its own refining system.
But traders said that most of the unplaced Nigerian barrels would probably head to the U.S. Gulf and Far East -- at substantial losses to sellers.
Traders assessed Bonny Light at just 10-20 cents above Dated Brent against the March OSP of +58 cents, but said it was hard to judge market values.
"Everything is getting so distressed it's hard to put a market value on anything. Things will get sold on a cargo by cargo basis," said one Nigerian crude contract lifter.
Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) normally seeks to set crude contract prices at about 11 cents below spot market values to cover business costs and profits.
But the company said on Friday that it would not revise March term price formulas despite heavy losses to customers.
--Rosalind Russell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5387
